title: CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE. On prayer: definition
latin: CAPUT VIGESIMUM PRIMUM, De precatione. Precatio est exercitium pietatis et militiae Christianae, quo fideles Deum Patrem de bonis dandis aut datis, malisque averruncandis aut averruncatis, impulsu Spiritus Sancti in nomine Iesu Christi petendo et gratias agendo compellant. Alias invocatio, alias adoratio dicitur. Per metaphoram sacrificium, suffimentum, vituli labiorum (Heb. 13:15). Est complexus et compendium fere omnium bonorum operum in homine renato.
english: Prayer is an exercise of piety and Christian warfare by which believers, at the Spirit's impulse and in Jesus Christ's name, address God the Father by petition and thanksgiving concerning goods to be given or already given, and evils to be averted or already averted.
It is also called invocation or adoration; metaphorically sacrifice, incense, calves of the lips. In the regenerate it is nearly a compendium of all good works.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): It stands as also called invocation or adoration; metaphorically sacrifice, incense, calves belonging toward ye lips. In ye regenerate it stands as nearly a compendium belonging toward all good works. — Prayer stands as an exercise belonging toward piety and Christian warfare by which believers, at ye Spirit's impulse and in Jesus Christ's name, address God ye Father by petition and thanksgiving concerning goods toward be given or already given, and evils toward be averted or already averted. — CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE. On prayer.

title: Impulsive causes; ends; object of petition
latin: IV. Causae impulsivae tres: voluntas Dei, necessitas nostra, exempla Christi sanctorumque. Finis: gloria Dei, unio et communio cum Deo, incrementum fidei. Objectum petitionum personale (pro nobis et aliis) aut reale (bona spiritualia et temporalia). Petendum in nomine Christi; solus Deus religiose adorandus.
english: IV. Three impulsive causes: God's will, our need, and the examples of Christ and the saints. The end: God's glory, union and communion with God, increase of faith.
What we ask for is personal (for ourselves and others) or real (spiritual and temporal goods). Ask in Christ's name; God alone is to be religiously adored.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): What we ask for stands as personal (for ourselves and others) or real (spiritual and temporal goods). Ask in Christ's name; God alone stands as toward be religiously adored. — IV. Three impulsive causes: God's will, our need, and ye examples belonging toward Christ and ye saints. Ye end: God's glory, union and communion with God, increase belonging toward faith.

title: Practical theorems 1–5
latin: XIV. Consectaria: 1. Preces in corde nasci, ore vero formari debent. 2. Christiani ad assidue orandum invitantur mandato, promissionibus, necessitatibus. 3. Nulla creatura sed solus Deus religiose adorandus est. 4. Etiamsi distincte Patrem, Filium, Spiritum invocamus, unus Deus adoratur. 5. Bona spiritualia petenda sine conditione quatenus ad Dei gloriam et salutem pertinent; temporalia cum conditione si Deo visum.
english: XIV. Corollaries: 1. Prayers should be born in the heart and formed with the mouth. 2. Christians are invited to continual prayer by command, promises, and needs.

3. No creature but God alone is to be religiously adored. 4. Even when we distinctly invoke Father, Son, and Spirit, one God is adored. 5. Spiritual goods are to be sought without condition insofar as they concern God's glory and salvation; temporal goods with the condition if God wills.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 3. No creature but God alone stands as toward be religiously adored. 4. Even when we distinctly invoke Father, Son, and Spirit, one God stands as adored. 5. Spiritual goods stand as toward be sought without condition insofar as they concern God's glory and salvation; temporal goods with ye condition if God wills. — XIV. Corollaries: 1. Prayers should be born in ye heart and formed with ye mouth. 2. Christians stand as invited toward continual prayer by command, promises, and needs.

title: Theorems 6–10; Cap.22 next
latin: 6. Bona spiritualia petenda a Deo sine conditione quatenus ad gloriam et salutem. 7. Fides mater verae invocationis parit fiduciam certae exauditionis, humilitatem, custodiam conscientiae. 8. Etiamsi Deus non semper largiatur desiderata sed neget aut differat, orando ducimur ad Dei unionem. 9. Bona quaedam pie deprecari licet. 10. Mali deprecatio. CAPUT VIGESIMUM SECUNDUM sequitur, De pace conscientiae.
english: 6–7. Faith, mother of true invocation, begets trust of certain hearing, humility, and custody of conscience.
8. Even when God does not always grant what is desired but denies or delays, by praying we are led to union with God. 9–10. Some goods may piously be prayed against; evils likewise deprecated.
CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO follows, On peace of conscience.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO follows, On peace belonging toward conscience. — 8. Even when God does not always grant what stands as desired but denies or delays, by praying we stand as led toward union with God. 9–10. Some goods may piously be prayed against; evils likewise deprecated. — 6–7. Faith, mother belonging toward true invocation, begets trust belonging toward certain hearing, humility, and custody belonging toward conscience.
